title: A Will for the Witness
premise: True-crime podcaster Oscar Dunmore has spent three years as the anonymous archivist of Hollow Creek's coldest case—the 1991 disappearance of a girl whose only witness vanished into protective silence. When a fresh corpse surfaces wearing clothes lifted from Oscar's own closet, she realizes someone has been watching her the way she watched everyone else. Decoding a ledger hidden in her late father's library index, she uncovers a protection racket that swallowed the town's leading families and made her father complicit in silencing the witness. The killer is Sheriff-elect Dale Voss, who has spent decades eliminating anyone who could testify; Oscar lures him into confessing on air during a live broadcast, trading her invisibility for justice at last.
about_author: Quentin Blackwood is the pseudonym of a former small-town newspaper reporter who covered two unsolved disappearances before leaving journalism for fiction. He writes from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where he keeps an alphabetized archive of every case that ever haunted him.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Oscar Dunmore records episode forty-seven of her podcast, cataloging the 1991 disappearance of Lily Marsh with clinical detachment. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: the comfort of control—she files grief in alphabetical order because feeling it would undo her.

chapters.title: A Body Wearing My Coat
chapters.summary: Hikers find a corpse in Miller's Hollow dressed in clothes stolen from Oscar's closet, down to her monogrammed scarf. Detective Rhea Calloway questions her. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: violation—the watcher realizes she has become the watched.

chapters.title: Three Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through Oscar's podcast tapes reveals how she inherited the case files from her late father, a court clerk. POV: Oscar via recordings. Emotional beat: unease—her father's notes contain gaps too deliberate to be accidents.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Oscar tracks down the case's sole witness, Ada Voss, supposedly relocated in 1992—and finds Ada living quietly under another name, terrified. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: dread—Ada recognizes the dead man's photo and goes white.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Searching her father's library, Oscar notices his card-catalog index encodes payments: initials, dates, amounts spanning thirty years. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve—her father wasn't just filing secrets; he was banking them.

chapters.title: Names That Built the Town
chapters.summary: The ledger implicates founding families: the Harrows, the Pembertons, and rising sheriff candidate Dale Voss—Ada's brother-in-law. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: vertigo—the town she archived was built on the crime she archives.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Knew
chapters.summary: Oscar identifies the victim: Martin Pell, a retired accountant who once audited the ledger's accounts. His laptop is missing. POV: alternating Oscar and Rhea. Emotional beat: acceleration—the murder isn't random; it's housekeeping.

chapters.title: An Offer of Protection
chapters.summary: Dale Voss visits Oscar's studio, charming and menacing, offering 'protection' and hinting he knows about her father's debts. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: cold fear masked by politeness—two predators circling over tea.

chapters.title: Ada Breaks
chapters.summary: Ada confesses what she saw in 1991: not Lily's abduction, but the cover-up—Lily alive, then gone, carried off in Voss family truck. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: guilt finally spoken after three decades of swallowing it.

chapters.title: The Missing Episode
chapters.summary: Someone deletes Oscar's cloud archive and ransacks her studio. Only her printed index survives, hidden in plain sight among her father's books. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: loss and defiance—they can burn the file but not the librarian.

chapters.title: Rhea's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Detective Calloway discovers her own captain took ledger money and must choose between the badge and the truth. POV: Rhea. Emotional beat: disillusionment—the law she served was bought long ago.

chapters.title: Lily's Grave
chapters.summary: Following ledger coordinates, Oscar and Ada find Lily Marsh's remains on Harrow farmland, buried the week after the 'disappearance.' POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief finally felt—the alphabetized case becomes a girl with a name.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ada explains why she stayed silent: Dale paid for her son's medical care, then threatened his life annually for thirty years. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: bitter clarity—survival was purchased, and the bill never stopped coming.

chapters.title: Election Week
chapters.summary: Voss surges in polls while Oscar's podcast is deplatformed by a hosting company with Harrow investments. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: suffocation—power doesn't need violence when it owns the infrastructure.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Martin Pell's missing laptop turns up—with its owner, dead again in the river, killed twice over to muddy the timeline. POV: Rhea. Emotional beat: horror—the killer is improvising now, which makes him dangerous and sloppy.

chapters.title: Trap or Testament
chapters.summary: Rhea secretly agrees to help Oscar, but warns that any evidence will be buried unless Voss confesses publicly. They plan a live broadcast trap. POV: Rhea. Emotional beat: fragile alliance—justice outside the law requires one insider willing to fall.

chapters.title: The Last Recording
chapters.summary: Oscar announces a finale episode: 'The Confession of Hollow Creek.' Voss, unable to resist controlling the narrative, agrees to appear. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: terror and purpose braided together—the mouse invites the cat on stage.

chapters.title: Live Air
chapters.summary: On air, Oscar plays the ledger, Ada's testimony, and a recording of Voss threatening Pell weeks before his death. Voss, cornered live, drops the charm and threatens Oscar on-mic. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: white-knuckle courage—three years of silence ending in one broadcast.

chapters.title: What Power Does Cornered
chapters.summary: Voss flees the studio, takes Ada hostage at the old courthouse, and demands the ledger originals. Oscar trades herself, stalling until Rhea arrives. POV: alternating Oscar and Rhea. Emotional beat: climax—survival means choosing to stop running.

chapters.title: The Fall of Dale Voss
chapters.summary: Rhea arrests Voss as his confession streams to thousands; the Harrow and Pemberton heirs are subpoenaed within hours. Voss, cuffed, tells Oscar her father sold Lily's silence willingly. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: victory shadowed—the price of survival was paid by everyone she loved.

chapters.title: Reckoning, Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Weeks later: indictments cascade, Ada testifies freely for the first time, and Oscar publishes her father's full ledger online. She mourns him honestly at last. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: grief integrated—invisibility was never safety, only slow surrender.

chapters.title: Episode Forty-Eight
chapters.summary: Oscar records her final episode—not about a cold case, but about the living: Lily's memorial, Ada's new life, Rhea's reform campaign. She signs off with her real name. POV: Oscar. Emotional beat: resolution—justice outside the law cost everything except the truth, and the truth was enough.
